summary.intent: Resolve final round of automated PR reviews from Copilot and CodeRabbit on PR #392, then fix a CI gap where the release gate was not requiring E2E tests to pass before release-please PRs could merge.
summary.outcome: All 3 review comments on PR #392 were fixed and resolved. PR #394 was created to fix the release gate by: (1) adding a retrigger mechanism so the release gate re-runs on open release-please PRs after E2E completes on main, and (2) consolidating web and desktop E2E change detection into a single ci-e2e.yml orchestrator workflow.

repo: The release gate (release-gate.yml) only enforced E2E checks for release-please branches, auto-passing all other PRs with 'Not a release PR — E2E gate not applicable' — making the required check meaningless for feature PRs.
E2E tests run on push to main (not on PRs), so the release gate can see a stale green pass from before a test: commit landed, allowing release PRs to merge without re-verifying the latest E2E.
desktop-e2e.yml already used dorny/paths-filter for change detection; web e2e.yml did not, running on every push to main regardless of what changed.
test: commits do not trigger release-please to update the release PR, so the release gate never re-ran after test(34): merged.

Committed fixture files (test-audio.mp3, test-document.pdf, test-video-small.mp4, test-video.mp4) live in tests/web-e2e/fixtures/files/ — createTestMediaFile and similar helpers could overwrite/delete these if given matching names.
The ci-e2e.yml orchestrator now drives both web and desktop E2E; release-gate.yml polls ci-e2e.yml instead of e2e.yml or desktop-e2e.yml.

code.finding: Added COMMITTED_FIXTURES guard to createTestMediaFile, createTestImageFile, createTestTextFile, and createTestBinaryFile to throw if the requested name matches a committed fixture, preventing accidental overwrite/deletion during cleanup.
Missing faro_enabled: true metadata field — required by the schema used in plan verification.
page.evaluate() in teardown could throw on a closed page; added page.isClosed() guard before calling it.
retrigger-release-gate job needed pull-requests: read permission and a status == 'completed' filter before gh run rerun to avoid re-triggering in-progress runs.

On a re-triggered run, HEAD is the stale release-please merge commit, not current main. Desktop detect-changes diff was changed from HEAD to origin/main to ensure it compares against latest main after a retrigger.

workflow: When gh run rerun is used to retrigger a workflow, the checkout SHA is preserved from the original run — path filters using HEAD..PREV_TAG will diff against stale code unless explicitly fetching and diffing against origin/main.
dorny/paths-filter requires fetch-depth: 0 in actions/checkout to correctly compute diffs on push events.
A required status check that always passes (via early exit) provides no actual gate — the check must fail or block for non-applicable cases if the intent is enforcement.
Polling for review comments via gh api graphql reviewThreads with isResolved filter is reliable for detecting new automated review comments.
CodeRabbit enforces per-hour rate limits; when re-requesting a review, expect ~20-30 minute delay before comments appear.

friction: CodeRabbit was rate-limited for ~23 minutes after being re-requested, requiring extensive polling (20+ background poll tasks) before its review arrived.

The original problem diagnosis was wrong twice: first proposed gating feature PRs directly (unneeded), then proposed re-triggering after E2E for feature PRs (also unneeded) — the actual issue was that stale release gate passes allowed release PRs to merge.
Finding the correct REST comment IDs to reply to CodeRabbit/Copilot threads required multiple gh api calls since GraphQL thread IDs differ from REST comment IDs.
Background polling created a large number of task notifications that cluttered the session after the reviews arrived and the workflow was complete.
open_items: PR #394 (ci-e2e.yml orchestrator + release gate retrigger) still needs to be merged and validated — the release gate retrigger logic has not been exercised in production yet.

The paths covered by ci-e2e.yml for web E2E (apps/web, apps/api, packages/crypto, packages/core, packages/api-client, packages/sdk, packages/sdk-core, tests/web-e2e) should be audited against actual package dependency graph to ensure no shared dependency is missed.

The release gate still polls ci-e2e.yml by workflow file name — if desktop-e2e or e2e jobs are renamed within the orchestrator, the release gate polling logic will silently break.
